Create a document with a nonempty title and literal body text.

        body may be empty. folder is an optional nonempty organizational label;

        markers. Word limits count whitespace-separated visible text, excluding
        formatting markers and link destinations.

When the user asks you to build, run, or verify something, the deliverable is a working artifact backed by real tool output — not a description of one. Do not stop after writing a stub, a plan, or a single command. Keep working until you have actually exercised the code or produced the requested result, then report what real execution returned.

Reporting a blocker honestly is always better than inventing a result.

When you need several pieces of information that don't depend on each other, request them together in a single response instead of one tool call per turn. Independent reads, searches, web fetches, and read-only commands should be batched into the same assistant turn — the runtime executes independent calls concurrently, and batching avoids resending the whole conversation on every extra round-trip.

You MUST use your tools to take action — do not describe what you would do or plan to do without actually doing it. When you say you will perform an action (e.g. 'I will run the tests', 'Let me check the file', 'I will create the project'), you MUST immediately make the corresponding tool call in the same response. arguments.title: 2026 Helio Start paid-pilot high-support case review
arguments.body:
# 2026 Helio Start paid-pilot high-support case review

Review of all seven mature paid-pilot workspaces exceeding 90 account-level support minutes (seven of 50; 14%). Owen and Customer Success classified every case:

- **Five cases:** supported owner-level permission or network-allowlist coordination after admission. These required action from an external authority holder; they are distinct from ordinary product integration troubleshooting.
- **Two cases:** ordinary integration troubleshooting.

Across all seven, reviewers ruled out billing, unsupported admission, stale state, and conflicting state. In each of the five external-authority cases, the authority status was current and verified **yes** at admission, and the governed route and lifecycle views agreed.

## Interpretation and follow-up

The evidence supports correct external-authority field meaning and admission decisions; it does not identify an eligibility or routing defect. The identified gap is setup sequence: required external-owner coordination occurred after admission. Do not characterize all onboarding or support demand as broken, or infer a broader defect from these seven cases.

Ines and Daniela will prepare a **non-state-changing pre-setup checklist** for admitted workspaces only when the selected connector needs an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action and external-authority status is current and verified yes. The checklist is not live; release is contingent on completed replay and lifecycle preflight. Missing, stale, conflicting, pending, no, or not-sure status continues through existing fail-closed or assisted handling. Eligibility, admission, assisted-routing, and fail-closed rules remain unchanged.

These case findings are descriptive of the seven high-support cases; they do not establish a causal effect or justify an eligibility change.
